messages.author: 4b85f40a0f87fa84
messages.subject: latent variable not updating
parts:
Hi Nimble folks,
I am trying to fit a relatively (at least conceptually) straight forward extension to an N-mixture model, where individuals belong to two fully observable groups and groups have different detection probabilities. Total abundance N follows a Poisson distribution and abundance in each group (N.b) is then a multinomial random variable with sample size = N. Here is a model code snippet:  

#abundance model
for (i in 1:nsites){
    lambda[i]<-exp(alpha + beta*hab[i]) #expected total abundance
    N[i]~dpois(lambda[i])                        ##total abundance
    N.b[i,1:2]~dmulti(bprob[1:2], N[i])     ##abundance in each of the two groups
  }

  #observation model
  for (j in 1:nsites){
    for (k in 1:K){
      for (i in 1:2){                              #loop over two groups of individuals
        Y[j,k,i]~dbin(dprob[i], N.b[j,i])  #dprob = detection probability for a given group; Y[i,j,k] are repeated counts in each group
      }}}

The model runs fine in Nimble (JAGS cannot handle the random sample size in the multinomial distribution), but N is not updated - it just sits at the initial value. Any ideas why that might happen? I checked and it is assigned a slice sampler; any reason a different sampler might do the trick?
Or am I overlooking something fundamental with this model?
I guess we could re-write it as essentially two separate N-mixture models, but I'd still be curious why this version won't work (or what we could do to make it work).
Thanks in advance!

  #detection
for (i in 1:2){

dprob[i] ~ dbeta(1,1)}

  #behavior

  # Likelihood, abundance

for (i in 1:nsites){

N[i]~dpois(lambda[i])

#observation model
  for (j in 1:nsites){
    for (k in 1:K){

Y[j,k,1:3]~dmulti(cprob[1:3], N[j])
      }}
  
  Ntotal<-sum(N[1:nsites])

                     data=data,#not necessary at this step
                     constants = consts, 
                     inits = inits())

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: latent variable not updating
parts:
Ok, sounds like you're off and running.

Just in case, or for future reference, here is an idea.

Let's say we have something like the following:

N[i] is number of individuals at site i.
Nobs[i, j, 1:2]  is number of individuals observed in each of states 1 and 2 during visit j to site i.
We assume there are some unobserved individuals during visit j to site i, namely N[i] - sum(Nobs[i, j, 1:2]) unobserved individuals.
We make an N-mixture assumption that N[i] ~ dpois(lambda)
We have multiple sites and multiple visits per site. 

So we would want a likelihood contribution from assuming that 
[Nobs[i, j, 1:2], N[i] - sum(Nobs[i, j, 1:2])] are multinomial with probabilities prob[1:3] and size N[i].  Here prob[3] is the probability of being unobserved.

The difficulty is that N[i] - sum(Nobs[i, j, 1:2]) is a deterministic calculation, and we can't make a deterministic node also be part of a stochastic declaration.  We could however do the following:

Nobs[i, j, 1:2] ~ dCustomMulti(prob[1:3], N[i])

and write dCustomMulti to internally calculate N[i] - sum(Nobs[i, j, 1:2]) and return the log probability of the desired 3-category multinomial.

I hope it makes some sense.

-Perry
